WHISTLEBLOWER AND NON-RETALIATION POLICY

Thornbury Federal Credit Union
Adopted by the Board of Directors on February 11, 2026

PURPOSE

This policy states how a director, officer, employee, volunteer, or contractor of Thornbury Federal Credit Union may report a concern about suspected wrongdoing, how the credit union will handle the report, and the protection from retaliation that every reporter has.

SCOPE

This policy covers a concern about any of the following: a violation of law or regulation; fraud, theft, or misappropriation; a material misstatement in a financial record or regulatory filing; a violation of the Code of Conduct or another credit union policy; a danger to health or safety; and the concealment of any of the foregoing.

HOW TO REPORT

A concern may be raised with the reporter's manager, with the Chief Compliance Officer, or with the Chair of the Audit Committee. A concern may also be reported through the independent hotline operated by Larkspur Ethics Line at (800) 555-0107 or larkspurethics.com/thornbury, which is available at all times and accepts anonymous reports.

Nothing in this policy limits any person's right to report a possible violation of law directly to a government agency, including the National Credit Union Administration, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, the Securities and Exchange Commission, and the Department of Justice, or to participate in an investigation by one. No prior notice to or approval by the credit union is required.

CONFIDENTIALITY

The identity of a reporter is kept confidential to the extent consistent with a fair and thorough investigation and with the credit union's legal obligations. A report may be made anonymously, though an anonymous report may be harder to investigate.

NO RETALIATION

The credit union prohibits retaliation against any person who in good faith reports a concern, participates in an investigation, or refuses to participate in conduct the person reasonably believes is unlawful. Retaliation includes termination, demotion, suspension, threat, harassment, reduction in hours or pay, negative evaluation, and any other adverse action.

A person who believes retaliation has occurred should report it to the Chief Compliance Officer or the Chair of the Audit Committee. A report made in good faith is protected even if the concern turns out to be unfounded. A report the reporter knows to be false is not protected and may itself be grounds for discipline.

INVESTIGATION

The Chief Compliance Officer acknowledges each report within five business days, determines who will investigate, and reports the substance and outcome to the Audit Committee at least quarterly. A concern involving the Chief Compliance Officer or a member of senior management is investigated under the direction of the Audit Committee. A concern involving accounting, internal controls, or auditing is reported to the Audit Committee immediately.

RECORDS

Reports and investigation records are retained for seven years and are accessible only to those with a need to know.

TRADE SECRETS

Under the Defend Trade Secrets Act of 2016, 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b), an individual is not held criminally or civilly liable under any federal or state trade secret law for disclosing a trade secret in confidence to a federal, state, or local government official or to an attorney solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law, or in a complaint or other document filed under seal in a lawsuit or other proceeding.

REVIEW

The Audit Committee reviews this policy at least annually and recommends changes to the Board.
